Why are we changing the prototype here?  Just call `add` from inside your discovery function to add a new ResponderInfo to be managed.
No, this should be done by the discovery functions themselves.
We should not be using GetManagedObjects to parse everything from entity-manager.  Use object mapper to find your specific type.
nit: use ERROR for consitency with the rest of the BMC code.  Don't use custom abbreviations like "EXCEP".

You should be looking for this directly.

Please add this type to phosphor-dbus-interfaces and use the class from there.
Use generated bindings to get all the properties and access them via variable names.
There is no reason to explicitly ask for the EM service here.  Other processes _could_ expose that configuration even if they don't today.  We generally do not want to hard-code service names.
Why?  I'd prefer we consider the "likelihood of bug" vs "noise to the reader".  It's not likely that someone inadvertently changes the values.

Do you know what this is doing for us?  It seems like we only need the object path once; I don't know why the original structures had two different properties for the object path but I left it until I saw more code for clarity.  

Is this suppose to be `object_path{objectPath}`?

SPDM TCP responder will have same value in both objects path variables but for MCTP 
there will be two object paths one comes from MCTP service and other from EM config.

Could we formulate this in one go?

```
spdmDiscovery.add(
  ResponderInfo(objectPath, sdbusplus::message::object_path{}, 
    TcpResponderInfo(properties.hostname, properties.port),
    TransportType::TCP));
```
make it much more human friendly - `TCP transport discovery completed`
I'd prefer not to have blanked catches like this.  Do we know what we're suppose to encounter?

This does not seems like a true util function to me - since its doing some filtering based on a service name ? would it be worth to leave it generic & put the check for EM where we consume the result ?
Do we really need the search root from `/` ? can't we do it from atleast `/xyz/openbmc_project/` or `/xyz/openbmc_project/configuration` ?
Do we need depth as an optional parameter?  Or do we think we'll always use 0?
copying the full map rather than emplace ?
I really don't like these catch-all exceptions.  Especially early in development wouldn't it be better to just fail quickly and fix the errors than hiding them in the journal?
I don't see any users of these?

This seems relatively complicated to me.  What are we returning?  Can we be clear somewhere in the documentation.

I think we just need one of these:

- std::map<object_path, vector<service_names>>
- std::map<service_names, vector<object_path>>
@archana.kakani@ibm.com @manojkiran.eda@gmail.com - I made some improvements to Archana's latest patch.  Please take a look.
